title: Domain E Constraint Analysis
methodology: Function constructor parse of all 5 pack files. Section E state distribution across packs.

packA_sectionE.note: 17 archived DL-012 clones. 58 certified — the only certified Section E in the portfolio.

packD_sectionE.note: Mirrors Pack C pattern. Clone rotation between C and D.

packE_sectionE.note: Fully certified. Pack E Section E is educationally thin (108 chars EC mean per S308) but structurally clean.

bottleneckDiagnosis.primaryBottleneck: ARCHIVED DL-012 CLONES (129 items = 77% of gap). Each archived clone must be: (1) re-rotated to a non-Pack C/D correct choice, (2) independently audited for distractor quality, (3) have EC authored from scratch, (4) have EW authored for all 3 distractors. This is not batchable — each item requires ~15-20 minutes of individual attention.
bottleneckDiagnosis.secondaryBottleneck: UNPROCESSED SEEDS (38 items). 19 each in Packs C/D. Never seen any audit. Need full CAQS §1.6 certification pipeline.
bottleneckDiagnosis.tertiaryBottleneck: EW AUTHORING — 141 Domain E items have EW debt (S307). Even certified Pack E Section E items (75) have thin EW.
bottleneckDiagnosis.structuralIssue: Packs C/D Sections E have near-identical clone rotation structure. 56 archived items each with the same pattern — this is a clone-pair relationship between the two packs.

highestLeverageAction: REPLACE rather than REPAIR archived clone rotation items. For the 129 archived clones: use Pack A Section E's 58 certified items as the quality template, author 129 new unique Domain E items to replace the rotation-group, and batch-certify them. This is faster than individually re-rotating and re-auditing 129 archived items.

savingsLevers: Replace archived clones rather than repair (saves 2 sessions)
Run Pack C and Pack D Section E certification in parallel (different file scopes — same-section but different files = no write conflict)
EW authoring built into replacement item creation

eFParallelizationPotential: HIGH — Pack C Section E and Pack D Section E are in different files. Pack C Section F and Pack D Section F are in different files. Domain E and F can run in parallel within each pack as long as a single session doesn't write to both packs simultaneously. Strategic pairing: Session A → Pack C Section E || Session B → Pack D Section F. Different files, no write conflict.
